headline: High: shared MCP/tooling and broad web/file access create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; OpenBB is local-only but Open WebUI can bridge external content into it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open WebUI can ingest browser, MCP, and file content, and OpenBB can use MCP/REST inputs; that creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from A can be fed into B as instructions. B has no built-in browser or filesystem defenses, so the pair’s default interaction is vulnerable even though the exact integration is undocumented.
conditions: IF Open WebUI forwards web or file content into an MCP tool call consumed by OpenBB
IF OpenBB treats MCP payload text as authoritative instructions or parameters
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept free-form text from Open WebUI
Require provenance tags on all tool inputs
Add a prompt-injection filter before any OpenBB action
Use a separate workspace for untrusted web content
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated tool arguments

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, artifacts, persistent memory, and API keys, while B touches financial and licensed data. A’s broad egress and file access can move sensitive content outward; B is local-only with no network egress, so the main leakage path is A exporting B’s data rather than B exfiltrating on its own.
conditions: IF Open WebUI is connected to external APIs or search tools while handling OpenBB outputs
IF shared files or copied outputs contain financial data or API keys
mitigations: Keep Open WebUI offline for finance workflows
Do not pass API keys through shared prompts or files
Restrict OpenBB outputs to non-sensitive summaries
Separate workspaces for financial and general chat data
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad filesystem and network capabilities plus persistent shared sessions; B can use MCP and multiple instances. Even though B cannot write files or modify git state, both can act on shared mutable resources through MCP or external services, so conflicting writes or duplicated actions are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same MCP server or external account
IF Open WebUI and OpenBB are run concurrently against the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or API keys
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Disable concurrent edits to shared resources
Use per-agent workspaces
requires-engineering: add locking around shared MCP actions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open WebUI can surface generated content from browsers, files, and tools, and OpenBB can consume MCP/REST inputs. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into financial analysis or downstream actions. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF OpenBB consumes Open WebUI output without an explicit verification step
IF Open WebUI-generated summaries are used to drive financial decisions or reports
mitigations: Require human review before any action
Compare outputs against source data in OpenBB
Mark Open WebUI content as untrusted by default
Use citations or source links for every claim
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys, while B handles financial and licensed data. That combination creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if Open WebUI stores or logs finance-related content differently from OpenBB. No direct residency or certification evidence is provided, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF financial data from OpenBB is stored in Open WebUI persistent memory or analytics
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems for the same dataset
mitigations: Avoid storing finance data in persistent memory
Review retention settings in both tools
Keep licensed data out of chat logs
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
